quiz.q: According to Karl Marx, why is renouncing religion insufficient to overcome human alienation?
options: Religion is merely part of the superstructure, so the underlying capitalist economic base must be transformed.
Alienation can only be eliminated when individuals raise their consciousness to merge with the universal spirit.
Religious institutions actively organize the working class into a revolutionary political party against factory owners.
Capitalism completely eliminates religious beliefs, replacing them with an objective scientific understanding of market relations.
quiz.why: Marx argued that religion is merely part of the superstructure. Therefore, alienation can only end by transforming the capitalist economic base.

quiz.q: How does Karl Marx distinguish true freedom in communism from bourgeois liberty in capitalism?
options: Bourgeois liberty provides freedom from material necessity, whereas communist freedom guarantees individual legal rights against society.
True freedom means liberation from material necessities, whereas bourgeois liberty is merely protective isolation from society.
True freedom requires competitive market wages, whereas bourgeois liberty forces individuals to labor beyond their capacities.
Bourgeois liberty abolishes private property, whereas communist freedom allows individuals to independently market their surplus goods.
quiz.why: Marx viewed bourgeois liberty as protective isolation from others, while true freedom requires liberation from basic material necessities.

quiz.q: Why did Vladimir Lenin deviate from Marx by introducing a vanguard Communist Party led by intellectuals?
options: Mature capitalist contradictions had already made Russian workers fully conscious of their revolutionary role.
He believed changing the economic base would automatically prevent power from concentrating among elites.
He believed Russian workers lacked spontaneous revolutionary consciousness, requiring middle-class intellectuals to manufacture it.
Marx explicitly instructed middle-class intellectuals to lead the state bureaucracy during the transition to communism.
quiz.why: Lenin believed Russian workers lacked revolutionary consciousness, so he used middle-class intellectuals to manufacture consciousness.

quiz.q: What does Marx mean by stating that material existence determines human consciousness rather than consciousness determining existence?
options: Universal spiritual consciousness evolves independently to construct the physical and economic structures of human society.
Legal and political institutions dictate the economic mode of production and assign individuals to classes.
Philosophical and religious ideas emerge first, subsequently creating society's material conditions and production relations.
Economic relations and material production form the base shaping society's legal, political, and philosophical ideas.
quiz.why: Marx argued that the economic base forms the foundation of society, which directly determines social, legal, and political consciousness.
